page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. The system is equipped with 128 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

The instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and database operations. Specifically, it achieves a multi-core Geekbench score in the top 10% and handles 144.9 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory read bandwidth reaches up to 7395.26 GB/sec for cached blocks and 466.64 GB/sec for uncached blocks.

While multi-threaded decompression and software compilation perform in the top tier, single-core CPU tasks and text processing fall into the average tier. Additionally, LLM text generation for small models is relatively weak, though text generation for medium and large models remains strong. This resource profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for high-throughput network applications, distributed databases, static web serving, and parallelized CPU workloads, whereas it is less suitable for tasks requiring local NVMe storage or hardware-accelerated graphics.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gn.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 128 GB of RAM and a high-speed 200 Gbps baseline network interface, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark results highlight top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and high-throughput database capabilities, as demonstrated by 144.9 million Redis SET operations per second and 116.84 GB/sec static web serving. However, single-core performance and small-model LLM text generation are more modest. This profile offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized, network-heavy workloads. It is highly suited for distributed databases, software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing.
